profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, with a ticker of NVDA. Its most recently reported annual revenue was $215,938,000,000 for the period ending January 25, 2026, as filed in a 10-K. The company develops hardware and software for accelerated computing, and its website focuses on AI model development and deployment tooling.

The company describes its Nemotron product line as a family of multimodal, open AI models built for agentic reasoning across tasks including advanced math, graduate-level science, and visual understanding. The site states that Nemotron models are available under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA. NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques alongside the models. Specific variants mentioned include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, described as helping agents complete specialized tasks faster, and NeMo Switchyard, described as routing steps to appropriate models. Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site as a voice behind the product's direction. Supporting tools mentioned include NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, and compatibility with open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. ServiceNow is named as a partner that has evaluated Nemotron models, specifically for visual question-and-answer accuracy.

The held facts track two NVIDIA products: Nemotron, categorized as an enterprise large language model family with synthetic data generation and self-hosted options, and NVIDIA NIM, categorized as inference microservices for deploying foundation models with enterprise GPU optimization. No litigation or MCP server entries are recorded for the company in the held facts.
